newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts comments on KLM 96/97 results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts comments on KLM 96/97 results.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines on Wednesday reported a net profit of 236 million guilders for the year to March 31, 1997, down from 547 million in 1995/96.
The 1996/97 result included a 290 million pre-tax provision.
Below is a collection of analysts' comments on the results.

"At first, I thought these results were more or less in line (with expectations). However, if you look at the breakdown, operating profit was quite disappointing. That's offset by the contribution from Northwest Airlines. Some of the cost items were higher than expected."
THIJS BERKELDER, HSBC VAN MEER JAMES CAPEL:

"There's no real news in the statement. Operating profit was somewhat lower than expected. The extraodinary charge was in line with our forecast. The positive surprise is the equity stake in earnings from Northwest Airlines. All the signals are that things will be mainly positive for KLM in the year coming. Fuel costs have dropped again, the dollar is higher again and load factors are at historic high levels. The only positive news they need now is a deal with Northwest."
